thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated tail latency and increased 5xxs for runtime-serving after rollout 2026-03-15T09:12Z. Metric windows show p99 generator latency up ~3.2x in slice 'canary-3', error rate spike from 0.2% -> 4.8%. Auto-created incident INC-277999 by pager.

alice (oncall): saw the page, joining. Observed a correlated drop in throughput from 1.1k rps -> ~650 rps for canary-3. Logs show a flurry of kernel fallback traces on the GPU nodes: "fallback_to_cpu_kernel:true". tagging eng-runtime and prod-sre. @caroline @dmitri please ack.

caroline (eng-runtime): Ack. I'm seeing scheduling churn around the batching controller — small micro-batches are proliferating, KV cache hit ratio for the live sessions down 18%. Canary commit is `ab4c9f2` (prefetch change + new batch planner heuristics). I suspect prefetch_v2 change causes more KV eviction and smaller batch sizes under typical tail traffic.

dmitri (prod-sre): Noted. Customer-facing metrics show a subset of long-running streaming requests getting retried which trips fallback and causes reprovisioning. Impact estimate: ~12% of requests see >2s tail delay, ~0.6% full failures (timeouts). Potential customer impact on Dedicated tenants using small-sequence interactive apps.

emma (support): FYI we have an incoming support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting slow responses for their chat feature at 09:15Z. They flagged a SLO breach on their side. I'll coordinate comms if we confirm it's our rollout.

alice (oncall): Plan: 1) flip the prefetched feature flag off for canary-3, 2) if that doesn't stabilize in 2 min, scale down canary-3 and re-route traffic to canary-1/2, 3) rollback commit ab4c9f2 if ongoing. Executing step 1 now: `/flag-toggle prefetched_v2 canary-3 off --reason "tail-latency spike"`.

deploy-bot: Command received: toggle `prefetched_v2` -> OFF for target canary-3. Change propagated to 4/4 nodes in slice. Time: 09:16:12Z.

caroline (eng-runtime): Good. Also opening a temporary batching window increase for canary-3 to let the batcher coalesce more tokens: `/runtime-config set canary-3.batch_target_ms 40`.

alice (oncall): Done. Watching telemetry...

[~60s later]

dmitri (prod-sre): Preliminary: p99 latency dropped from 3.2x to ~1.4x after flag flip and batch_target_ms bump. 5xx rate down to 1.1%. KV cache hit ratio recovering slowly. Looks promising but not back to baseline yet. Keeping traffic on canary-3 for now to validate.

caroline (eng-runtime): Logs still show intermittent kernel fallback events, but much less frequent. I want to push a temporary guard in the runtime: if fallback_count > 3 within 10s, drop to fallback-safe model variant that has lower memory pressure. Pushing patch `hotfix/277999-fallback-guard`.

deploy-bot: Hotfix `hotfix/277999-fallback-guard` deployed to canary-3 (rolling). 3/3 processes updated. Time: 09:18:55Z.

emma (support): AcmeCorp says response times improved around 09:19Z. They're asking for a short RCA and mitigation ETA.

alice (oncall): Good signal. I'm going to do a 15m handoff to ben because I need to step into an ops call. Summarizing state for handoff: root cause suspected: prefetched_v2 caused aggressive prefetch eviction and micro-batching policy causing KV churn -> increased GPU memory pressure -> kernel fallback to CPU. Immediate mitigations: prefetched_v2 OFF, batch_target_ms increased to 40ms, hotfix guard deployed. Metrics trending down but still ~10% above baseline for p99.

ben (oncall-next): Taking handoff. I'll keep watch for 30m, prepare rollback plan if it regresses. What's the rollback command for the release? 

caroline (eng-runtime): Rollback is `deploy rollback release/2026-03-15-ab4c9f2 --target canary-3`. If we need to rollback globally, we can run the same against `release/2026-03-15` across slices. We should prefer kill-switch + hotfix first to avoid global churn.

ben (oncall-next): Copy. I'll also pre-warm fallback-safe variants in canary-1/2 so we can shift traffic without cold start risk.

alice (oncall): One more ask: get an SLO impact estimate for the last 30m and prepare a customer-facing blurb for AcmeCorp. Emma can you draft? Keep it short: cause, mitigation, ETA for full remediation.

emma (support): Draft: "We observed a service-side latency regression tied to a recent canary rollout affecting a portion of requests. We've disabled the new prefetch optimization, applied a runtime guard, and increased batching to stabilize throughput. Early metrics show improvement; we expect a full return to baseline in ~30-60 minutes while caches warm. We're continuing to monitor and will update within 30 minutes." Thoughts?

dmitri (prod-sre): Good. Add quant: "p99 latency reduced by ~55% after mitigation; error rate down from 4.8% -> 1.1%". Also mention mitigation steps so engineering-savvy contacts can understand.

emma (support): Updated blurb with numbers. Sending to AcmeCorp now. :thumbsup:

[~10 minutes]

caroline (eng-runtime): After additional logs, root cause extra detail: the prefetch_v2 path added a speculative KV pin that, under certain sequence length distributions, caused the LRU window to shrink aggressively. That produced higher cache eviction churn and smaller batch formation. The runtime's memory accounting then flipped to a safe path (CPU kernels) to prevent OOM, which is expensive and caused the tail latency. We'll include exact heap profiles in the postmortem.

dmitri (prod-sre): For tracking: opening INC-277999-rootcause and assigning to eng-runtime as P0. Tagging postmortem owners: caroline, alice, and platform lead.

alice (oncall): Handing off fully to ben at 09:23Z. Ben, please escalate to release leads if there's another spike. I'm reachable if needed.

ben (oncall-next): On it. Monitoring dashboards: no regression in last 10m, p99 trending down. I'll open a canary-blocking flag in the release pipeline so `release/2026-03-15` does not proceed to additional slices until eng-runtime signs off. `/release-pipeline hold release/2026-03-15 --reason "canary instability"`.

deploy-bot: Pipeline hold applied to release/2026-03-15 by ben. Time: 09:24:02Z.

caroline (eng-runtime): Next steps for remediation: revert prefetch_v2 heuristics, add a KV eviction guard + metrics, tune batch planner to prefer slightly larger windows under medium tail variance. I'll open PRs and link in the incident ticket.

dmitri (prod-sre): We'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow to cover fix rollouts and customer comms. For now, keep the hold and keep prefetched_v2 OFF by default for slices until patch merged.

emma (support): AcmeCorp confirmed performance stable and appreciated the quick update. Marking the customer notification as sent in INC-277999.

alice (oncall): back online from my ops call. Thanks Ben, Caroline, Dmitri, Emma. I'll follow the postmortem thread. Closing my shift.

ben (oncall-next): Continuing watch. Reopen if we see spike >1.5x baseline p99 or error rate >2%.

incident-bot: Incident INC-277999 status: mitigated. Timeline, artifacts, and links: INC-277999-rootcause (ticket), logs-slice-canary-3 (s3://redwood-logs/277999/canary-3), rollback-runbook updated. Assigned owners: eng-runtime (caroline), prod-sre (dmitri), oncall (ben).
